summary: Intermittent rerank order variance for short multilingual queries after quantization-path autoscale
description:
Issue summary: Customer reports intermittent changes in top-k order returned by the /rerank endpoint for short multilingual queries. The behavior appears when their workload autoscaled between instances using quantized kernels and instances running fp16/fp32 kernels.

Impact: Affects production search relevance for ~2% of queries (short queries in non-English languages). Customer sees top-1 and top-3 swaps for otherwise near-tied candidates, leading to user-facing relevance regressions. Customer flagged as enterprise with SLA; issue started 2026-03-09 22:00 UTC.

Environment: prod (us-east), Dedicated cluster (mixed-precision autoscaling enabled). Models: redwood/embed-compact-v2 (quantized variant on GPU pool) and redwood/reranker-alpha.

Steps to reproduce (customer supplied):
1) POST /embed for 3 short queries in Portuguese/Spanish/Hindi (examples attached).
2) POST /rerank with embeddings against same candidate set (N=50).
3) Repeat 10x across a traffic window where autoscaler triggers GPU quantized pool.
4) Observe intermittent swaps in top-k order between runs.

Expected: Deterministic rerank ordering for identical inputs and pinned model versions.

Actual: Top-k ordering changes when requests are routed to quantized-serving path vs non-quantized path. Not all queries affected; sensitivity correlated with near-tie cosine scores (~delta < 0.002).

Attached logs: customer provided request IDs, sample payloads, and exported cosine score lists. Linked dashboards show small but consistent shift in embedding L2 norms (~0.010–0.025) when quantized path is used.
comments: 2026-03-10 08:12 UTC - Asha Patel (Support): Acknowledged. Escalating to SRE and embeddings team. Requested request-ids and sample payloads.

2026-03-10 09:03 UTC - Customer (LinguaSearch): Provided 12 request ids, three sample queries in PT/ES/HI and two candidate sets. Noticed variance after 2026-03-09 22:00 UTC coincident with increased traffic. Attached CSV of cosine scores.

2026-03-11 11:25 UTC - Liam O'Connor (Eng): Preliminary repro in our staging by toggling quantized kernels. Observed small mean L2 norm delta between quantized and fp16 paths. Opening investigation notes.

2026-03-12 15:40 UTC - SRE (I. Nguyen): Autoscaler logs show pool switching events at 2026-03-09 21:58:42 UTC for customer cluster; GPU pool served ~22:00–22:45 UTC, then fell back. Added routing trace ids.

2026-03-13 10:55 UTC - Data (E. Morales): Compared cosine distributions for affected queries: median delta 0.0018, 95th pct delta 0.012. Near-tie pairs (delta < 0.002) flipped ~45% of the time when path changed.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis 1: Quantized kernel introduces slightly different scaling/rounding for output vectors which changes normalized cosine ordering for near-tie items. Multilingual short queries have sparser token coverage causing larger relative variance.
Hypothesis 2: Tokenization differences across language scripts create subword distributions that amplify small numeric differences after quantization. Confirmed with Spanish and Hindi test cases.

Reproduction: Deterministic repro achieved by alternating calls between a forced-quantized serving instance and an fp16 instance using the same payloads. Mean embedding L2 norm (fp16) = 1.002, (quantized) = 0.990 for one test set (delta 0.012).
Observed: Normalization is not consistently re-applied in rerank pipeline when embeddings are ingested from different paths. Some code paths assume unit-normalized embeddings from upstream.
Temporary mitigation test: Client-side L2 renormalization immediately prior to rerank restores deterministic ordering in our repro. Workaround suggested to customer while we patch server-side.
next_steps: 1) Engineering: Add deterministic unit-normalization step in rerank ingestion path to remove reliance on upstream numeric equivalence (priority P0 internal change).
2) Runtime: Audit quantized kernel post-processing to ensure output scaling matches fp16 reference within tighter tolerance for production models.
3) QA: Create unit tests that alternate serving backends and assert stable top-k ordering for near-tie inputs (include multilingual short tokens).
4) Customer communication: Share workaround (client-side L2 renorm) and ETA for server-side fix. Schedule follow-up on 2026-03-14.
